# Skrami — agent guide

Skrami (https://skrami.app) is an instant, no-signup, sticky-note scrum board:
realtime, shared by URL. This file is the wire-protocol reference for AI agents
and scripts. The whole API is one WebSocket plus one HTTP POST — anything that
can open a WebSocket can read a board, create and move cards, and appear in
presence next to the humans.

There are no accounts and no API keys. The board URL is the only credential —
treat it as a capability and never post it anywhere public. A human shares a
board with an agent by sharing the URL, nothing else.

There is no REST API. Reading a board = connect, say hello, receive a snapshot.
Writing = send ops. Both are described below, with copy-paste recipes at the end.

## Boards and URLs

A board lives at:

    https://skrami.app/b/<flavor>-<id>

The id is the final hyphen-separated token: exactly 7 chars from the alphabet
`abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789` (no i, l, o, 0, 1). Everything before it is
"flavor" — a display name the server ignores. `/b/<id>` alone works too.

## Connect

    wss://skrami.app/b/<id>/ws

The first message you send MUST be a hello:

    {"t":"hello","cid":"<your-client-id>","v":0,"pending":[]}

- `cid`: your client identity — any non-empty string ≤ 64 chars. Use a stable
  one per agent (e.g. "agent-claude-rsedykh") so your op sequence numbers
  survive across sessions.
- `v`: the board version you last saw; send 0. The server always replies with
  a full snapshot regardless.
- `pending`: ops to apply immediately on connect (see one-shot recipe below);
  send [] if you have none.
- On password-protected boards add `"token":"<token>"` (see Passwords).

The server replies:

    {"t":"snapshot","board":{...},"version":N,"protected":false,"yourSeq":S}

`board` is the complete current state (a whole board is a few KB). `yourSeq` is
the highest op seq the server has ever accepted from your cid — your next op
must use a seq greater than that. Boards are small; there is no delta protocol.

Other messages the server may send at any time:

    {"t":"ops","ops":[...],"version":N}      // edits by you or others
    {"t":"presence","users":[{"cid","name","editing"}]}
    {"t":"authRequired"}                     // then close 4003 — get a token
    {"t":"deleted"}                          // then close 4001 — board deleted

Keepalive: send the literal string `ping`; the server answers `pong`.

## Board state (what the snapshot contains)

    Board  { id, name, columns: [{id,name}], stories: {id: Story},
             tasks: {id: Task}, createdAt, deletedAt, ts, uploadcareKey? }
    Story  { id, title, note, attachments, orderKey, ts }     // a row
    Task   { id, storyId, column, title, assignee, priority,
             note, attachments, orderKey, doneAt, ts }        // a sticky note

- Stories are rows; columns run left to right. Column ids `todo` and `inprog`
  are permanent; `done` is implicit, always last, and never appears in
  `columns[]` — move a task to column `"done"` to complete it (`doneAt` is
  stamped server-side).
- `ts` maps field names to last-write timestamps — conflict resolution is
  last-write-wins per field; you can ignore it when reading.
- `attachments`: `{url, name, isImage}` — https URLs only; files themselves
  live on Uploadcare, not in Skrami.
- The in-app JSON export is exactly this Board object.

## Writing: ops

Send:

    {"t":"ops","ops":[{"cid":"<your cid>","seq":1,"ts":1723200000000,"op":{...}}]}

Envelope rules:

- `seq`: strictly increasing per cid, starting above the snapshot's `yourSeq`.
  An op with a stale seq is dropped SILENTLY.
- `ts`: epoch milliseconds (your current time; the server clamps it). It is the
  last-write-wins tiebreak per field.
- ≤ 500 envelopes per message.
- The server echoes every applied op back to everyone INCLUDING you:
  the echo is your ack. No echo = dropped (stale seq or failed validation).
- Ops are idempotent absolute writes ("set column to X"), never relative
  ("move left"), so retries are safe.
- An op referencing a missing target (create a task in a story someone just
  deleted) is accepted and echoed but changes nothing — trust the snapshot +
  echoes, not your intent.

## Op catalog

IDs for things you create are client-generated: any string ≤ 64 chars, UUIDs
recommended. Limits: title ≤ 2000 chars, note ≤ 4096 (plain text, URLs get
auto-linked), assignee ≤ 120, column name ≤ 60, ≤ 10 attachments each
(https URL ≤ 600 chars), orderKey ≤ 64. Over-long text is truncated.

    {"t":"story.create","id","title","orderKey"}
    {"t":"story.set","id","set":{title?,note?,attachments?}}
    {"t":"story.move","id","orderKey"}
    {"t":"story.del","id"}                    // also deletes the row's tasks

    {"t":"task.create","id","storyId","column","title","assignee",
     "priority":false,"note":"","attachments":[],"orderKey"}
    {"t":"task.set","id","set":{title?,note?,assignee?,priority?,attachments?}}
    {"t":"task.move","id","storyId","column","orderKey"}
    {"t":"task.del","id"}

    {"t":"col.add","id","name","index"}       // id must not be "done"
    {"t":"col.set","id","name"}
    {"t":"col.move","id","index"}
    {"t":"col.del","id"}                      // refused for todo/inprog or non-empty

    {"t":"board.setName","name"}              // becomes the URL flavor: must match
                                              // ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,48}[a-z0-9])?$
    {"t":"board.del"}                         // DELETES THE BOARD (30-day grace)

DESTRUCTIVE OPS — `board.del`, `story.del`, `col.del`, and mass `task.del`
remove other people's work. Send them only when a human explicitly asked for
that exact action. The same goes for the `setPassword` / `removePassword`
WebSocket messages, which exist but are not an agent's business.

## Ordering (orderKey)

Stories (and tasks within a cell) sort by `orderKey` as plain strings, ties
broken by id. To position an item, pick any string that sorts strictly between
its neighbors, using chars `0-9A-Za-z`, never ending in `0`:

- first item ever: `"V"`
- append after last key `"z"`: `"zV"`
- between `"a0V"` and `"a0X"`: `"a0W"`

## Presence — be a visible teammate

After hello, announce yourself:

    {"t":"presence","name":"Claude"}          // name ≤ 60 chars

You appear in the board's presence roster like any human. Set `assignee` on
cards you create to your name — cards are colored by assignee, so your work is
visibly yours. While editing an existing task, optionally send
`{"t":"editing","id":"<taskId>"}` (and later `{"t":"editing","id":null}`) so
humans see an "is editing" badge and don't collide with you.

## Password-protected boards

If the snapshot never arrives and you get `{"t":"authRequired"}` (close code
4003), the board has a password. Exchange it for a token:

    POST https://skrami.app/b/<id>/auth
    {"password":"..."}

    200 {"token":"..."}     // put it in the hello: {"t":"hello",...,"token":"..."}
    403 {"error":"wrong"}
    429 {"retryAfter":N}    // exponential backoff after 3 misses — do NOT retry blind

Tokens are long-lived but rotate when someone changes the password — on
authRequired, re-auth once with the password you were given.

## Creating a board

Generate a 7-char id from the alphabet above, then just connect and send ops —
a board persists the moment it receives its first op. (Humans do the same by
clicking "Create board"; empty boards are never stored.)

## Recipes

Read a board (Node ≥ 22, no dependencies — also works in Deno/Bun/browsers):

    const ws = new WebSocket("wss://skrami.app/b/<id>/ws");
    ws.onopen = () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({t:"hello", cid:"my-agent", v:0, pending:[]}));
    ws.onmessage = (e) => {
      const m = JSON.parse(e.data);
      if (m.t === "snapshot") { console.log(JSON.stringify(m.board)); ws.close(); }
    };

One-shot write, single round trip: put your envelopes in `pending` of the hello
itself — they are applied before the snapshot is taken, so the snapshot you get
back confirms your write. Remember: if you reuse a cid, seqs must keep growing;
after storage loss, reconnect once with `pending:[]`, read `yourSeq`, continue
from there.

Live collaboration: keep the socket open, apply incoming `ops` to your local
copy of the board, send `ping` every ~10 s.

## Stability

This document describes the live protocol as of 2026-08-09 and is updated with
it. The protocol is small and stable, but not versioned — if a message you
receive has a `t` you don't know, ignore it.
